source.title: List homomorphism problems for signed trees

accepted.question_text: For a fixed signed graph H with possible loops, where signed-graph homomorphisms are considered up to switching of the input signature, consider List-S-Hom(H): given an input signed graph G and a list L(v) of allowed target vertices for each vertex v of G, decide whether there is a signed-graph homomorphism from G to H sending every v to an element of L(v). Which fixed signed graphs H make List-S-Hom(H) polynomial-time solvable, and which make it NP-complete? Can the polynomial side be described by a natural graph-theoretic structure analogous to bi-arc graphs for unsigned graph list homomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Definition 3. Let Hb be a fixed signed graph. The list homomorphism problem List-S-Hom(Hb) takes as input a signed graph Gb with lists L(v) ⊆ V (H) for every v ∈ V (G), and asks whether there exists a homomorphism f of Gb to Hb such that f(v) ∈ L(v) for every v ∈ V (G).

We conclude that our problems List-S-Hom(Hb) fit into the general constraint satisfaction framework, and therefore it follows from [9, 31] that dichotomy holds for problems List-S-Hom(Hb). We therefore ask which problems List-S-Hom(Hb) are polynomial-time solvable and which are NP-complete.

The structure of the signed trees in the polynomial cases is interesting, suggesting that the class of general signed graphs for which the problems are polynomial may have nice structure, analogous to the so-called bi-arc graphs (which characterized the polynomial cases of list homomorphisms to unsigned graphs).

It seems difficult to give a full combinatorial classification of the complexity of list homomorphism problems for general signed graphs. We have accomplished this for signed trees (with possible loops).

accepted.question_text: For List-S-Hom(H) restricted to fixed target signed graphs H that are irreflexive, bipartite, and contain at least one bicoloured edge, and after excluding cases where the signed core already has more than two edges, which such targets H yield polynomial-time solvable signed list homomorphism problems and which yield NP-complete problems?
accepted.context_brief: Irreflexive bipartite signed targets with bicoloured edges

evidence.quote: We have observed that List-S-Hom(Hb) is NP-complete if the s-core of Hb has more than two edges. Thus we will focus on signed graphs Hb whose s-cores have at most two edges.

Thus we consider irreflexive signed graphs. The s-core is still too big if the underlying graph has an odd cycle. So in this case it remains to classify the irreflexive bipartite signed graphs that contain a bicoloured edge. Even this case is complex. We explore homomorphisms to irreflexive bipartite signed graphs in a companion paper.
